title: Dwyer--Kan weak exponentials and the homotopy-limit criterion
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and the Dwyer--Kan model structure and its derived limits, colimits and enriched mapping sets as in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus], in fixed universes. This model structure is combinatorial; its trivial fibrations are exactly the enriched functors surjective on objects and trivial Kan fibrations on every mapping simplicial set. Cofibrations have the left lifting property against these functors. Its diagram categories admit projective model structures for every small ordinary index category, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Cartesian multiplication preserves homotopy colimits indexed by small partially ordered sets: for any fixed simplicial category $D$, the derived functor $D\times^h-$ sends such homotopy colimit cocones to homotopy colimit cocones.

Let $K=K_0\cup\{\infty\}$ be a small partially ordered set obtained by adjoining a largest element to a small partially ordered set $K_0$, possibly empty. Put $B=\{(a,b)\in K^{\mathrm{op}}\times K:b\leq a\}$. Suppose given an object $X$ of $\mathrm{sCat}$, functors $Y:K\to\mathrm{sCat}$, $Z:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sCat}$, $P:B\to\mathrm{sCat}$, and spans
$$ Z(a)\times Y(b)\longleftarrow P(a,b)\longrightarrow X $$
functorial in $(a,b)$. Assume each left map represents a homotopy product of $Z(a)$ and $Y(b)$. Assume for $a=b$ the span is a weak exponential: the induced morphism $[Z(a)]\times[Y(a)]\to[X]$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ induces bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T,Z(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(T\times^hY(a),X)$$
for every small simplicial category $T$. If the cone $Y$ exhibits $Y(\infty)$ as a homotopy colimit of $Y|_{K_0}$, then $Z$ exhibits $Z(\infty)$ as a homotopy limit of $Z|_{K_0^{\mathrm{op}}}$. This is a homotopy limit in the full Dwyer--Kan model structure, not just a limit of its homotopy category.
